speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you describe the location and severity of your flank pain, and have you noticed any changes in your urination, such as blood or increased frequency?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any nausea, vomiting, or chills during this episode? I would also like to check your blood pressure and examine your abdomen for tenderness.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the rash appear shortly after starting amoxicillin, and have you noticed any swelling in your face, hands, or feet since then? I will also check your abdomen for any tenderness or organ enlargement.

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Culture. I suspect acute interstitial nephritis triggered by your recent antibiotic use, so I need to check for white blood cells and eosinophils in your urine.

text: RESULTS: Leukocyturia Present, Bacterial Culture Negative, Cytospin Stained With Hansel’s Solution 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of eosinophils in your urine, combined with the rash and fever following antibiotic use, strongly suggests acute interstitial nephritis. To confirm the extent of kidney involvement, I need to check your blood chemistry. REQUEST TEST: Serum Creatinine and BUN.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your elevated creatinine and urea levels confirm acute kidney injury, which, combined with the eosinophilic urinary casts and recent drug exposure, points to acute interstitial nephritis. I will now review your imaging to rule out other causes. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: The sinus symptoms improved, but the flank pain and fever stayed. The rash happened during the antibiotics and then resolved after the change in medication.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging shows no structural abnormalities, confirming that your acute kidney injury is not due to obstruction or infection. Given the classic triad of fever, rash, and eosinophiluria following antibiotic exposure, I am confident in my conclusion. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
